observations.code_quote: - **Rewrite.** On the next run, a pre-extraction activity copies the live Delta table into a sibling temp table under the new scheme, recomputing `_ph_partition_key` for every row. It then does a crash-safe swap: delete live → server-side copy temp → verify row count → delete temp. The copy (`pipelines/core/repartition_stream.py`) never opens a dataset over the whole table, because a dataset keeps the parquet footer of every file it has scanned and its memory grows with each file. It plans from the add actions of the loaded version and reads one source file at a time: small files whole, a few ahead on worker threads, large files by row group. It writes through a capped set of open parquet files, one per target partition, and commits them as add actions with stats. One memory-governor slot sizes every buffer, so memory depends on that budget, not on the table's size, its file count or the rows already written. Commits land on source-file boundaries, at least once per checkpoint interval, and each records the source files it completes.

Adding phase markers and checkpoints could help recovery and make the swap safer and more observable.
